Quick read and assessment from Product: short answer — feasible with Dedicated + operational changes, but there are important scope details. Notes below.

1) Traffic & model footprint
- Need a breakdown of model family(s) they plan to use (Llama3, mix of smaller encoder models, embeddings) and expected qps by hour. The latency target is plausible for smaller/quantized models on Dedicated GPUs but more aggressive for full-size LLMs.

2) Availability interpretation
- 99.995% monthly uptime means ~2.2 minutes of downtime/month. We need to clarify allowed maintenance windows, planned upgrades, and what counts as SLA breach (regional outage vs single-AZ).

3) Operational controls we require
- Multi-AZ deployment (Active/Standby) with automated failover and explicit fallback model variants (smaller model) if instance capacity saturated.
- Prefix/KV caching enabled for chat workloads to reduce token load and improve p95.
- Request routing policy pinned to Dedicated pool; automatic fallback to a compatible hosted variant only with prior written permission.

4) Pilot proposal (recommended)
- 30-day pilot on Dedicated with 2 redundant zones, 25% cold standby capacity. Measure latency and failover performance; tune batching and kernel configs.
- After pilot, propose a phased SLA: 99.9% trial SLA for first 90 days, then re-evaluate for 99.995% if pilot metrics meet targets.

5) Cost & timeline
- Short lead: provisioning Dedicated pool (standard capacity) ~2-4 weeks; full standby + multi-zone ~4-6 weeks.
- Expect material uplift (~40-80% on top of baseline Dedicated pricing) depending on standby sizing and replication strategy. Exact numbers in attached estimate.

Attachments: capacity_estimate_Q2.xlsx (capacity scenarios + cost estimates)

Questions for Sales/Legal:
- Are they willing to accept phased SLA and explicit exception language for planned maintenance?
- Do we have permission to include a fallback to a lower-cost hosted variant during extreme capacity events?

Happy to sketch technical appendix for procurement.
